nodes.summary: For every finite directed graph $G$ with ordered adjacency lists and every source vertex $s$, the result of the executable breadth-first search from $s$ equals the result of the list model of breadth-first search from $s$: both report the same distance (or none) for every vertex and the same first-discovery order.
nodes.title: The executable BFS agrees with the list model

nodes.summary: Given a natural number $n$, an adjacency function assigning to each vertex $i < n$ an ordered list of vertices among $0, \dots, n-1$, and a source vertex $s < n$, this is the result of breadth-first search from $s$ on the finite directed graph with vertex enumeration $0, 1, \dots, n-1$ and these adjacency lists.
nodes.title: Breadth-first search on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$

nodes.summary: Given a finite directed graph $G$ with ordered adjacency lists and a source vertex $s$, the list model keeps a list of processed pairs and a queue of pairs $(v, d)$ of a vertex and a distance, starting with no processed pairs and the queue $[(s, 0)]$. It performs one round per vertex of $G$: if the queue is empty, nothing changes; otherwise the front pair $(u, d)$ is removed from the queue and recorded as…
nodes.title: List model of breadth-first search

nodes.summary: For every finite directed graph $G$ with ordered adjacency lists and every source vertex $s$, the output of breadth-first search with parents from $s$ in $G$, with its cost and its predecessor table forgotten, equals the result of ordinary FIFO breadth-first search from $s$ in $G$: the same distance table and the same first-discovery order.
nodes.title: Breadth-first search with parents returns the ordinary BFS result

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph with vertex list $V$ and adjacency lists $\mathrm{adj}(u)$, and let $s$ be a vertex. The cost of breadth-first search with parents from $s$, counting dequeue attempts, adjacency checks, enqueues and parent writes, is at most $3|V| + \sum_{u \in V} |\mathrm{adj}(u)|$, where adjacency lists are counted with repetitions.
nodes.title: Linear bound on the cost of BFS with parents

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph with vertex list $V$ and adjacency lists $\mathrm{adj}(u)$, let $s$ be a vertex, and let $L$ be the list of vertices in the order in which breadth-first search from $s$ discovers them. The cost of breadth-first search with parents from $s$, counting dequeue attempts, adjacency checks, enqueues and parent writes, equals $|V| + \sum_{u \in L} |\mathrm{adj}(u)| + |L| + (|L| - 1)$,…
nodes.title: Exact cost of BFS with parents

nodes.summary: Given a finite directed graph $G$ on a vertex type $V$, with ordered adjacency lists, and a source vertex $s$, this runs first-in-first-out breadth-first search from $s$ for $|V|$ rounds. The queue starts with $s$ at distance $0$. Each round tries to dequeue a vertex $u$; if it succeeds, it scans the neighbors of $u$ in adjacency-list order, and each neighbor not yet discovered gets distance one more than $u$,…
nodes.title: Breadth-first search with parent pointers

nodes.summary: Given a finite directed graph $G$ with ordered adjacency lists and a source vertex $s$, breadth-first search keeps a FIFO queue of pairs $(v, d)$ of a vertex and a distance and a table of discovered vertices with their distances, starting with the queue $[(s, 0)]$ and $s$ discovered at distance $0$. It performs one round per vertex of $G$: if the queue is empty, nothing changes; otherwise it dequeues the front pair…
nodes.title: Breadth-first search

nodes.summary: A breadth-first search forest on a vertex type $V$ consists of a breadth-first search result, namely a partial distance function from $V$ to the natural numbers and a list of vertices, together with a partial predecessor function from $V$ to $V$. For a search from a source vertex $s$, these are meant to give the distance from $s$ of each reachable vertex, the reachable vertices in first-discovery order, and the…
nodes.title: Breadth-first search forest

nodes.summary: A breadth-first search result on a vertex type $V$ consists of a distance function, assigning to each vertex either a natural number or none, and a list of vertices. They are meant to record the shortest distance from the source (none when the vertex is unreachable) and the vertices in first-discovery order.
nodes.title: Result of breadth-first search

nodes.summary: For every finite directed graph $G$ with ordered adjacency lists, all vertices $s$ and $v$, and every natural number $d$, breadth-first search from $s$ reports distance $d$ for $v$ if and only if there is a walk of exactly $d$ edges from $s$ to $v$ in $G$ and $d \le k$ for every natural number $k$ such that there is a walk of exactly $k$ edges from $s$ to $v$.
nodes.title: BFS reports exactly the shortest walk length

nodes.summary: For every finite directed graph $G$ with ordered adjacency lists and all vertices $s$ and $v$, breadth-first search from $s$ reports some distance for $v$ (rather than none) if and only if $v$ is reachable from $s$ in $G$.
nodes.title: BFS reports a distance exactly for the reachable vertices

nodes.summary: For every finite directed graph $G$ with ordered adjacency lists and every vertex $s$, the distances reported by breadth-first search from $s$, listed along its first-discovery order, form a nondecreasing sequence, where a vertex without a reported distance counts as $0$.
nodes.title: BFS discovers vertices in nondecreasing distance

nodes.summary: For every finite directed graph $G$ with ordered adjacency lists and all vertices $s$ and $v$, the vertex $v$ occurs in the first-discovery order of breadth-first search from $s$ if and only if $v$ is reachable from $s$ in $G$.
nodes.title: BFS lists exactly the reachable vertices

nodes.summary: For every finite directed graph $G$ with ordered adjacency lists and every vertex $s$, no vertex occurs twice in the first-discovery order of breadth-first search from $s$.
nodes.title: BFS discovers each vertex at most once

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph given by adjacency lists, and let $s$ and $v$ be vertices. Following the saved parents of the breadth-first search forest of $G$ from $s$ back from $v$ towards $s$ returns no path if and only if $v$ is not reachable from $s$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Path reconstruction fails exactly at unreachable vertices

nodes.summary: For every breadth-first search forest $F$ and every vertex $s$, following the saved parents of $F$ from $s$ back to $s$ returns the one-vertex path $[s]$. This holds for every forest, including one whose discovery order is empty.
nodes.title: Path reconstruction at the source

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph given by adjacency lists, let $s$ and $v$ be vertices, and suppose that following the saved parents of the breadth-first search forest of $G$ from $s$ back from $v$ returns a list $P$ of vertices. Then $P$ starts at $s$ and ends at $v$, each vertex of $P$ after the first has the preceding vertex as its saved parent, $G$ has an edge from each vertex of $P$ to the next, no vertex…
nodes.title: Reconstructed BFS paths are shortest paths

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph given by adjacency lists, and let $s$ and $v$ be vertices with $v$ not reachable from $s$ in $G$. Following the saved parents of the breadth-first search forest of $G$ from $s$ back from $v$ costs exactly $2$, counting one unit for each comparison with $s$, each parent lookup and each vertex prepended to the path: one comparison of $v$ with $s$ and one lookup of the missing parent…
nodes.title: Cost of path reconstruction for an unreachable vertex

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph given by adjacency lists, let $s$ and $v$ be vertices, and suppose breadth-first search from $s$ reports distance $d$ for $v$. Following the saved parents of the breadth-first search forest of $G$ from $s$ back from $v$ costs exactly $3d + 2$, counting one unit for each comparison with $s$, each parent lookup and each vertex prepended to the path.
nodes.title: Cost of path reconstruction for a reachable vertex

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the predecessor function of a breadth-first search forest, let $n$ be the length of its discovery order, and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. Starting from $v_k = t$, this walks back along $p$, setting $v_{i-1} = p(v_i)$, until it reaches a vertex $v_0$ that tests equal to $s$, and returns the list $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k$. It returns no list if the walk meets a vertex that does not test equal to $s$ and has…
nodes.title: Path reconstruction from BFS parents

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph given by adjacency lists and let $s$ and $v$ be vertices. If a list of vertices starts at $s$, ends at $v$, and each of its vertices after the first has the preceding vertex as its saved parent in the breadth-first search forest of $G$ from $s$, then no vertex occurs twice in the list.
nodes.title: Saved-parent chains are simple

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph given by adjacency lists, and let $s$ and $v$ be vertices with $v$ reachable from $s$ in $G$. There is exactly one list of vertices that starts at $s$, ends at $v$, and in which each vertex after the first has the preceding vertex as its saved parent in the breadth-first search forest of $G$ from $s$.
nodes.title: Each reachable vertex has a unique saved-parent chain

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph with ordered adjacency lists, $s$ a vertex, and $F$ the predecessor forest computed by breadth-first search with parents from $s$ in $G$. If $F$ records $p$ as the predecessor of a vertex $v$, then there is a natural number $d$ such that $F$ records distance $d$ for $p$ and distance $d + 1$ for $v$.
nodes.title: A BFS parent is one step closer to the source

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph with ordered adjacency lists, $s$ a vertex, and $F$ the predecessor forest computed by breadth-first search with parents from $s$ in $G$. If $F$ records $p$ as the predecessor of a vertex $v$, then $G$ has a directed edge from $p$ to $v$, that is, $v$ occurs in the adjacency list of $p$.
nodes.title: BFS parents are joined by graph edges

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph with ordered adjacency lists, $s$ a vertex, and $F$ the predecessor forest computed by breadth-first search with parents from $s$ in $G$. For every vertex $v \ne s$, the predecessor that $F$ records for $v$ is the first vertex $u$, in the first-discovery order of ordinary FIFO breadth-first search from $s$ in $G$, whose adjacency list contains $v$; if no vertex in that order has…
nodes.title: The BFS parent is the first discovered in-neighbour

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph with ordered adjacency lists, $s$ a vertex, and $F$ the predecessor forest computed by breadth-first search with parents from $s$ in $G$. A vertex $v$ has no recorded predecessor in $F$ if and only if $v = s$ or $v$ is not reachable from $s$ along directed edges of $G$.
nodes.title: Exactly the source and the unreachable vertices have no BFS parent

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph given by adjacency lists and let $s$ and $v$ be vertices. In the breadth-first search forest of $G$ from $s$, there is no sequence $v = x_0, x_1, \dots, x_k = v$ with $k \ge 1$ in which each $x_i$ is the saved parent of $x_{i+1}$.
nodes.title: The saved-parent relation is acyclic

nodes.summary: For every finite directed graph $G$ given by ordered adjacency lists and every vertex $s$ of $G$, breadth-first search in $G$ from $s$ reports a distance for $s$ itself, and that distance is $0$ edges.
nodes.title: Breadth-first search places the source at distance zero
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
